  NATURE CENTER FINANCING

  Recommendation: That the City Council 1) Adopt Resolution No. 2612 authorizing
  the issuance of tax-exempt obligations, if needed, for the purpose of financing the
  new George F Canyon Nature Center Project, and 2) Direct staff to initiate the
  process to obtain a credit rating to support potential short-term financing for cash flow
  management.

Administrative Services Director Whitehead provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

Consultant Mark Young, KNN Consulting, explained the benefit of obtaining a Credit Rating to
support potential short-term financing to address cash flow concerns, in response to COUNCIL
MEMBER SCHACHTER. Mr. Young further explained that doing so provides flexibility in
financing options.

COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF confirmed that the City’s pension obligation is considered by the
rating agencies and would be positively noted.

Mr. Young further summarized that the proposed reimbursement resolution gives the City the
flexibility and option to finance the funding gap for the Nature Center Project, should the City
need to do so.

9.  OLD BUSINESS

A.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION ACTION ITEM: OVERVIEW AND
  EVALUATION OF PILOT PROGRAM FOR ALL-DAY TENNIS CLUB COURT
  RESERVATIONS AT ERNIE HOWLETT PARK

  Recommendation: That the City Council review and approve 1) Continuing weekday
  afternoon staffing at the tennis club to support ongoing facility management and
  programming; and 2) Implementing the proposed hybrid structure of weekday
  afternoon reservations, paid pickleball drop-in open play programming (for a cost of
  $5 per person per day/visit), and free Friday afternoon court use for both tennis and
  pickleball players to begin in January 2026 which would provide ample time for public
  outreach and staff training.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas provided a staff report (as per the agenda
material).

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
NOVEMBER 18, 2025
 Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas explained that the proposed hybrid structure is
based on feedback received from members of the public during the community meeting and
Park and Activities Commission meeting, in response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas explained what the structure looked like before
the pilot program began and outlined the benefits of having a City staff person on site, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas explained that the courts are always open to the
public for use, and open courts can be reserved in person if they are open, or by phone, in
response to COUNCIL MEMBER HUFF.

Community Services Supervisor Pinuelas explained the difference between “open play” and
“community play,” as well as the thought process behind free open play on certain days and
paid open play on others in the proposed schedule, in response to MAYOR STEGURA.

COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER confirmed that although the proposed schedule is not a
pilot program, there would be the opportunity for staff to make changes based on demand
and needs.

Public comment was invited in-person in the Council Chamber, via email and via eComment.
Public testimony was received via e-Comment as part of the public record, as well as from
Michelle Grahada, resident of Lomita, who provided suggestions for more open play
opportunities.

  COUNCIL MEMBER SCHACHTER moved, seconded by COUNCIL MEMBER
  HUFF, TO APPROVE AS FOLLOWS BY THE FOLLOWING ROLL CALL VOTE:

  APPROVE: 1) CONTINUING WEEKDAY AFTERNOON STAFFING AT THE
  TENNIS CLUB TO SUPPORT ONGOING FACILITY MANAGEMENT AND
  PROGRAMMING; AND 2) IMPLEMENTING THE PROPOSED HYBRID
  STRUCTURE OF WEEKDAY AFTERNOON RESERVATIONS, PAID
  PICKLEBALL DROP-IN OPEN PLAY PROGRAMMING (FOR A COST OF $5
  PER PERSON PER DAY/VISIT), AND FREE FRIDAY AFTERNOON COURT
  USE FOR BOTH TENNIS AND PICKLEBALL PLAYERS TO BEGIN IN
